title: Context Windows
description: Work within 200K tokens. Understand the constraints of long-context models.

title: Long-Term Memory
description: Database-backed recall. How agents remember across sessions.

title: Vector Embeddings
description: Semantic search in docs. Find relevant context at scale.

title: Building Knowledge Bases
description: RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation). Ground agents in your data.

title: Memory Hygiene
description: Forgetting, expiring, and correcting what an agent remembers.

title: Context Engineering
description: Decide what goes into the model's view at each step and what stays out — treating context as a budget spent every single API call, not a one-time allowance; separating what must be present from what can be fetched on demand; using position and ordering deliberately instead of by accident; compacting history to keep decisions and drop noise; and measuring what a context is actually costing instead of assuming it's fine.

title: Retrieval
description: Fetch the right information from a corpus at the moment the agent needs it — understanding the actual problem retrieval solves versus stuffing everything into context, chunking without losing meaning, embeddings and semantic search mechanically, when keyword search beats vectors, and evaluating retrieval quality separately from whatever the model does with what it retrieved.

title: Long-Term Memory
description: Let an agent remember across runs without accumulating garbage — deciding what's actually worth persisting past a single session, writing memory as a deliberate decision rather than an automatic log, retrieving what's relevant now rather than whatever's merely similar, resolving contradiction and staleness instead of silently accumulating both, and treating stored memory about a real person as the privacy question it actually is.

title: State and Durability
description: Make long runs survive restarts, crashes and days off — distinguishing state that must be checkpointed from state that's safe to lose and recompute, checkpointing after every step instead of only at the end, resuming from exactly where a run left off instead of redoing or silently double-doing work, making side-effecting steps idempotent so a retry after a crash is provably harmless, and designing runs that can legitimately span days without holding a process open the whole time.

title: Grounding and Citation
description: Make an agent's claims traceable to a source you can check — testing every claim against whether it actually points somewhere, generating citations that are real and locatable rather than plausible-sounding, saying "the source doesn't say" instead of filling retrieval gaps with confident general knowledge, handling conflicting sources honestly instead of silently picking one, and verifying grounding automatically instead of spot-checking outputs by hand.
